summary:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive digital space museum that explores the legacy of human-made equipment left behind during space exploration. It brings together eight carefully researched exhibits from the Moon, Mars, and deep space, including lunar landers, rovers, scientific instruments, and spacecraft.

Users can explore equipment profiles, discover their scientific purposes and achievements, follow interactive mission timelines, and investigate documented locations through a planetary atlas. The project also includes a learning section with quizzes, and educational challenges.

By combining NASA mission records, historical photographs and interactive storytelling, the project makes space exploration history easier to understand and explore. Its goal is to show that even when missions end, the knowledge and discoveries they leave behind remain valuable for future generations.
details:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive digital space museum that documents eight pieces of human-made equipment from space exploration. The collection covers historical missions involving the Moon, Mars, and deep space.

The application provides several interactive experiences:

  • Equipment Collection: Users can search, filter, and explore eight equipment profiles, learning about their purpose, engineering, scientific contributions, mission history, and documented status.
  • Planetary Atlas: An interactive Moon and Mars coordinate visualization allows users to explore documented equipment locations and mission sites. It distinguishes confirmed equipment coordinates from approximate mission-site markers.
  • Mission Timeline: Users can explore important events throughout the history of the featured missions.
  • Learning Lab: An educational section provides quizzes, explanations, equipment comparisons, and self-guided discovery activities.
  • Sources and Transparency: Each exhibit contains references supporting its historical and scientific information. The application also provides a searchable source library and an AI-use disclosure.

Data and research

The project uses NASA mission records, scientific information, historical photographs, and documented location coordinates. Sources include NASA's Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), NASA Science, NASA/JPL, and NASA's Image and Video Library.

Rather than presenting unsupported assumptions as facts, the application identifies uncertainties in mission dates, equipment locations, and mission status. It also distinguishes between last communication, mission retirement, and confirmed equipment locations.

Technology

The application was developed using SvelteKit 2, Svelte 5, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, D3 Geo, and Lucide icons. It uses a static deployment architecture hosted on Vercel, with a locally curated dataset and locally stored, credited NASA photographs.

We also implemented automated data validation and browser testing using Node.js and Playwright.

Benefits and intended impact

The project transforms historical mission records into an accessible and engaging learning experience. It helps students and space enthusiasts understand the engineering behind space exploration, appreciate the scientific discoveries made by earlier missions, and explore the legacy of equipment that remains beyond Earth.

The creative approach is to treat this history as a digital museum rather than a conventional collection of articles, connecting scientific evidence with interactive maps, timelines, visual storytelling, and educational activities.
